subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For systemd-managed Gateway runs, should provider keys from config `env` be treated as daemon-runtime credentials, service-environment material to write out, or unsupported in favor of per-agent auth profiles?
rationale: The source paths show documented config-env setup, marker-only service rendering, and process-env-based status diagnostics, but changing any one of them affects credential persistence, status semantics, and existing managed-service expectations.

options.title: Runtime contract plus diagnostics
options.body: Keep provider secrets out of generated systemd files, ensure the daemon applies the same config snapshot at startup, and add status/health/docs that expose config-path or runtime-env drift clearly.

options.title: Service materialization
options.body: Write selected config-env provider keys into a secure EnvironmentFile or SecretRef-backed service path, accepting the larger credential persistence surface and requiring upgrade/security proof.

options.title: Auth profiles only
options.body: Document config env as CLI/config-only for managed services and steer Kimi Coding users to `models auth --agent ... paste-api-key`, accepting a behavior change for users following the current docs example.

recommendation.title: Runtime contract plus diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep provider secrets out of generated systemd files, ensure the daemon applies the same config snapshot at startup, and add status/health/docs that expose config-path or runtime-env drift clearly.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history owner across config env application, service-env render policy, and model-status auth diagnostics.
